code='''def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    # Read palette from the repeated colored bar, ordered left-to-right or top-to-bottom.
    counts={}
    for row in grid:
        for v in row:
            if v: counts[v]=counts.get(v,0)+1
    # motif color has a standalone component; palette color may include 1, so detect motif from upper area
    cells=[(r,c) for r in range(h//2) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]]
    mc=max(set(grid[r][c] for r,c in cells),key=lambda v:sum(grid[r][c]==v for r,c in cells))
    pts=[(r,c) for r,c in cells if grid[r][c]==mc]
    r0,r1=min(r for r,c in pts),max(r for r,c in pts); c0,c1=min(c for r,c in pts),max(c for r,c in pts)
    mask=[[grid[r][c]==mc for c in range(c0,c1+1)] for r in range(r0,r1+1)]
    # palette strip is the repeated three-cell band in the lower area
    pcells=[(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] and not (r0<=r<=r1 and c0<=c<=c1)]
    # infer palette ordering by scanning the repeated band across columns
    # for horizontal palette, take one value per column from its three repeated rows
    palette=[]
    for c in range(w):
        vals=[grid[r][c] for r in range(h) if grid[r][c] and (r,c,grid[r][c]) in pcells]
        if vals:
            v=vals[0]
            if v not in palette: palette.append(v)
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]; mh=len(mask); mw=len(mask[0]); start=(h-len(palette)*mh)//2
    for i,v in enumerate(palette):
        for dr in range(mh):
            for dc in range(mw):
                if mask[dr][dc]: out[start+i*mh+dr][c0+dc]=v
    return out
'''
